subtopic: Shares — Face Value, Market Value, Brokerage
stem: Shri Maniklal has purchased 300 shares of F.V. ₹100, for M.V. ₹120. Company has paid dividend at 7%. Complete the following activity to find the rate of return on his investment.
solution:
F.V. \(= ₹100\), Number of shares \(= 300\), Market value \(= ₹120\).
(a) Sum invested \(= MV \times \text{No. of shares} = 120 \times 300 = ₹36{,}000\).
(b) Dividend per share \(= FV \times \text{rate of dividend} = 100 \times \dfrac{7}{100} = ₹7\).
\(\therefore\) Total dividend received \(= 300 \times 7 = ₹2{,}100\).
(c) Rate of return \(= \dfrac{\text{Dividend income}}{\text{Sum invested}} \times 100 = \dfrac{2100}{36000} \times 100 = 5.83\%\) (approx).

stem: A two digit number is to be formed from the digits 2, 3, 5 without repetition of the digits. Complete the following activity to find the probability that the number so formed is an odd number.
solution:
Let \(S\) be the sample space of all two-digit numbers formed from 2, 3, 5 without repetition.
\(S = \{23, 25, 32, 35, 52, 53\}\), so \(n(S) = 6\).
Event A: the number so formed is an odd number.
\(A = \{23, 25, 35, 53\}\), so \(n(A) = 4\).
\(P(A) = \dfrac{n(A)}{n(S)} = \dfrac{4}{6} = \dfrac{2}{3}\).

subtopic: Solving by Formula and Completing the Square
stem: Solve the following quadratic equation by using formula method: \(x^2 - 2x - 3 = 0\).

A committee of two members is to be formed from three boys and two girls. Find the probability of the following events:
Event A: At least one girl must be a member of the committee.
Event B: Committee must be of one boy and one girl.
solution:
Let the boys be \(B_1, B_2, B_3\) and the girls be \(G_1, G_2\). Total ways of choosing 2 members from 5 \(= \dbinom{5}{2} = 10\), so \(n(S) = 10\).
Event A (at least one girl): the committees with no girl (both boys) number \(\dbinom{3}{2} = 3\). So \(n(A) = 10 - 3 = 7\), and \(P(A) = \dfrac{7}{10}\).
Event B (one boy and one girl): \(n(B) = 3 \times 2 = 6\), and \(P(B) = \dfrac{6}{10} = \dfrac{3}{5}\).

subtopic: Mean, Median and Mode of Grouped Data
stem:
In a general store the prices of different articles and its demand is shown in the following frequency distribution table. Find the Median of the prices.

| Price in Rupees | No. of Articles |
|---|---|
| Less than 20 | 140 |
| 20–40 | 100 |
| 40–60 | 80 |
| 60–80 | 60 |
| 80–100 | 20 |
solution: Taking the first class as 0–20, the classes and frequencies are 0–20 (140), 20–40 (100), 40–60 (80), 60–80 (60), 80–100 (20). Total \(N = 140 + 100 + 80 + 60 + 20 = 400\), so \(\dfrac{N}{2} = 200\). Cumulative frequencies: 0–20 \(\to 140\), 20–40 \(\to 240\). The median class is 20–40, with \(L = 20\), \(cf = 140\), \(f = 100\), \(h = 20\). Median \(= L + \dfrac{\frac{N}{2} - cf}{f} \times h = 20 + \dfrac{200 - 140}{100} \times 20 = 20 + \dfrac{60}{100} \times 20 = 20 + 12 = 32\). The median price is ₹32.
